content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge uses a cited text's failure to name whose body is the channel as the reason to mark the point UNDERDETERMINED.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"`a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED` — I weighed whether the omission in Acts 2:30 is forbidden single-verse nonspecification or a permissible two-sense openness; the judge treats it as openness without identifying two senses.","why":"The D5 finding is UNDERDETERMINED because Acts 2:30 does not specify the body-channel, which is exactly the single-verse omission K-S2 forbids as a ground for that result."}
